title: High Order Geometric Channels for Nonlinear Transport in Bloch Bands
authors: Sami Farrag, Eugene Mele, Tony Low
abstract: We develop a geometric perturbation theory of Bloch states for perturbations coupling via the interband Berry connection. The gauge-invariant Bargmann trace builds the dressed dispersion and connection order by order as a hierarchy \(Q^{(N)}\), starting with the quantum geometric tensor. Higher members encode multiband geometry beyond the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Connected amplitudes control vertex-order corrections, while strict-order corrections reduce to disconnected products. For a uniform electric field we find the fully coherent, purely geometric sector of the third-order response.
summary: This work establishes a sophisticated geometric perturbation theory for nonlinear electronic transport in Bloch bands. It extends standard descriptions by calculating higher-rank tensors that capture complex multiband geometry. The key achievement is the derivation of intrinsic third-order conductivity channels using rigorous diagrammatic and recursive methods.
main_problem: The paper develops a geometric perturbation theory to calculate nonlinear transport coefficients, specifically charge conductivity, in electronic systems described by Bloch bands.
main_result: It derives the full set of intrinsic third-order conductivity channels ($\sigma^L$ and $\sigma^W$) that are purely geometric, showing how higher-rank tensors encode physics beyond simple quantum metrics.
method: The methodology involves constructing a hierarchy of geometric tensors ($Q^{(N)}$) using the Bargmann trace and employing diagrammatic techniques to separate vertex-order (dressed) corrections from strict-order (bare gap) corrections.
model_or_system: The system is electronic matter described by Bloch wavefunctions in periodic potentials, analyzed via perturbation theory applied to interband couplings induced by an external electric field.
key_observables: Third-order charge conductivity components ($\sigma_{abc;d}$), including intrinsic channels like the gradient of a three-band energy loop ($\sigma^L$) and curvature corrections ($\sigma^W$).
important_parameters: Electric field strength ($E$), perturbation order ($N=3$ for conductivity), and relaxation time ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of equilibrium distribution functions for intrinsic channels, leading to fully geometric results independent of scattering rates in the $	au 	o 0$ limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bargmann expansion up to fourth order, diagrammatic rules for connected/disconnected tensors ($Q^{(N)}$), and specific diagrams showing strict-order corrections needed for second- and third-order conductivity calculations.
paper_structure: The paper builds from developing the general geometric perturbation theory via the Bargmann trace hierarchy ($\Lambda(N)$) to deriving algebraic recursion relations, then applying these tools to calculate energy corrections (BW formalism), and finally collecting terms into specific, physically interpretable nonlinear transport channels for conductivity.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the rigorous geometric framework—using higher-order invariants beyond curvature—provides powerful mathematical machinery applicable to any system where geometry dictates response, such as quantum optics or open quantum systems dynamics.
